cohort: The study participants were 18 patients (13 vaginal deliveries and 5 caesarean sections) who experienced refractory postpartum hemorrhage.
finding: The bilateral cervix apex clamping (BCAC) procedure was found to be a simple, safe, and effective non-invasive method with a 94.4% overall success rate in decreasing bleeding in patients with refractory PPH.
mod_finding: The BCAC procedure achieved a 92.3% success rate for vaginal delivery cases and 100% for caesarean section patients, demonstrating its effectiveness across both modes of birth.
